items.question: Why must the pilot never push the cyclic forward to descend or to terminate a pull-up, as in an airplane?
options: It may produce a low-G (near weightless) condition that can result in a main rotor blade striking the cabin
items.explanation: Safety Tip 1 (see SN-11): never push the cyclic forward to descend or to end a pull-up — this may produce a low-G condition which can result in a main rotor blade striking the cabin. Always use the collective to initiate a descent.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: SAFETY TIPS 1 (p.10-1); Safety Notice SN-11

items.question: What does Safety Tip 2 say about the low fuel caution light?
options: It is a normal working fuel gage
Never intentionally allow the fuel quantity to become so low in flight that the low fuel caution light comes on
It may be ignored for 10 minutes
It only applies to bladder tanks
items.explanation: Safety Tip 2 (see SN-15, 'Fuel Exhaustion Can Be Fatal'): never intentionally allow the fuel quantity to become so low in flight that the low fuel caution light comes on.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: SAFETY TIPS 2 (p.10-1); Safety Notice SN-15

items.question: According to Safety Tip 9, most hard landings are survivable as long as what?
options: The rotor is not allowed to stall
items.explanation: Safety Tip 9: never allow rotor RPM to become dangerously low. Most hard landings will be survivable as long as the rotor is not allowed to stall.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: SAFETY TIPS 9 (p.10-2); Safety Notices SN-10, SN-24

items.question: What does Safety Tip 10 warn against, especially at high altitude?
options: Takeoffs or landings downwind — the loss of translational lift can cause the aircraft to settle into the ground or obstacles
items.explanation: Safety Tip 10: never make takeoffs or landings downwind, especially at high altitude; the resulting loss of translational lift can cause the aircraft to settle into the ground or obstacles.

items.question: How does Safety Tip 11 say vortex ring state can be avoided?
options: By always reducing rate of descent before reducing airspeed
By adding full power on the approach
items.explanation: Safety Tip 11 (see SN-22): a vertical descent or steep approach, particularly downwind, can cause the rotor to fly into its own downwash — vortex ring state — where even maximum power may not stop the descent. Avoid it by always reducing rate of descent before reducing airspeed.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: SAFETY TIPS 11 (p.10-2); Safety Notice SN-22

items.question: Per Safety Tip 12, the helicopter is stable on its landing gear as long as ground contact is made how?
options: Vertically, or with the aircraft moving forward
items.explanation: Safety Tip 12: the helicopter is stable on its landing gear as long as ground contact is made vertically or with the aircraft moving forward. Contact while moving rearward or sideward could cause damage and possibly a rollover.

items.question: Per Safety Tip 13, when operating above 3000–4000 ft, RPM must be controlled with what?
options: The collective — throttle/collective correlation is not effective and governor response is slow
items.explanation: Safety Tip 13: above 3000–4000 ft the throttle is frequently wide open and RPM must be controlled with the collective. Correlation is not effective and governor response is fairly slow; it may be necessary to roll the throttle off as collective is lowered to prevent an overspeed.

items.question: Per Safety Tip 15, why should the R22 not be landed in tall dry grass?
options: The exhaust is low to the ground and very hot, so a grass fire may be ignited
items.explanation: Safety Tip 15: do not land in tall dry grass — the exhaust is low to the ground and very hot; a grass fire may be ignited.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: SAFETY TIPS 15 (p.10-3); Safety Notice SN-17

items.question: Per Safety Tip 17, why should a magneto check never be attempted in flight?
options: If one magneto is malfunctioning and the pilot grounds the other, the engine may stop completely
items.explanation: Safety Tip 17: never attempt a magneto check in flight. If one magneto is malfunctioning and the pilot grounds the other, the engine may stop completely. If a magneto malfunction is suspected, leave the key in BOTH and land as soon as practical.

items.question: Per Safety Notice SN-9, what is the most effective way to stop a dynamic rollover?
items.explanation: SN-9: once started, dynamic rollover cannot be stopped by opposite cyclic alone. Quickly applying down collective is the most effective way to stop a dynamic rollover.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: Safety Notice SN-9 (p.10-6)

items.question: Per Safety Notice SN-9, how should hovering autorotations be practised to avoid dynamic rollover?
options: Into the wind, and never when the wind is gusty or over 10 knots
items.explanation: SN-9: always practice hovering autorotations into the wind and never when the wind is gusty or over 10 knots; never hover close to fences, sprinklers, bushes or lights a skid could catch; always use a two-step liftoff.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: Safety Notice SN-9 (p.10-6)

items.question: Per Safety Notice SN-10, what conditioned reflex must every pilot have for any low-RPM situation?
options: Instantly add throttle and lower collective to maintain RPM
Enter autorotation and turn into wind
items.explanation: SN-10: a primary cause of fatal light-helicopter accidents is failure to maintain rotor RPM. Every pilot must have his reflexes conditioned to instantly add throttle and lower collective to maintain RPM in any emergency. In forward flight, aft cyclic also helps recover RPM.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: Safety Notice SN-10 (p.10-6)

items.question: Per Safety Notice SN-10, if RPM drops 10%, how much power is lost?
options: About 10% (power available is directly proportional to RPM)
items.explanation: SN-10: power available from the engine is directly proportional to RPM. If RPM drops 10%, there is 10% less power — raising collective to stop the settling pulls RPM down further, causing the ship to settle even faster.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: Safety Notice SN-10 (p.10-6)

items.question: Per Safety Notice SN-11, how is the rotor reloaded to allow lateral cyclic to stop a low-G roll?
options: Immediately apply a gentle aft cyclic, avoiding any large cyclic inputs
items.explanation: SN-11: the rotor must be reloaded before lateral cyclic can stop any roll. To reload the rotor, immediately apply a gentle aft cyclic, but avoid any large cyclic inputs. Roll severity increases with airspeed and when lightly loaded.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: Safety Notice SN-11 (p.10-6)

items.question: Per Safety Notice SN-1, what should the pilot do if the mixture control is inadvertently pulled in flight?
options: Lower the collective and enter autorotation; if altitude permits, push the mixture in and restart with the left hand — do NOT disengage the clutch
items.explanation: SN-1: if the mixture control is inadvertently pulled, lower the collective and enter autorotation. If there is sufficient altitude, push the mixture in and restart the engine using the left hand. Do not disengage the clutch.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: Safety Notice SN-1 (p.10-6)

items.question: Per Safety Tip 7, what should the pilot do if an unusual sound or vibration begins in flight?
options: Continue to destination and report it
Make a safe landing and have the aircraft thoroughly inspected before flight is resumed
Increase airspeed to smooth it out
items.explanation: Safety Tip 7: a change in the sound or vibration of the helicopter may indicate an impending failure of a critical component. If an unusual sound or vibration begins in flight, make a safe landing and have the aircraft thoroughly inspected before resuming flight.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: SAFETY TIPS 7 (p.10-2); Safety Notices SN-28, SN-39

items.question: What does Safety Tip 14 say about slowing the rotor during shutdown and about the tail rotor?
options: Use collective pitch to slow the rotor quickly
Do not use collective pitch to slow the rotor (blades may strike the tailcone), and never slow or stop the rotors by grabbing the tail rotor
Apply the rotor brake immediately at engine stop
Grab the tail rotor only if the rotor brake fails
items.explanation: Safety Tip 14: do not use collective pitch to slow the rotor during shutdown — it produces lift that can disengage droop-stop friction and let blades strike the tailcone. Also, do not slow or stop the rotors by grabbing the tail rotor, which can damage the tail rotor drive.

items.question: Which R22 POH safety topic must be knowledge-based only and never practised or demonstrated in flight?
items.explanation: A caution in PILOT KNOWLEDGE AND PROFICIENCY: never practice or demonstrate low-G in flight; low-G training should be knowledge based only. In-flight practice of low RPM, power failures and autorotations should only be conducted under instructor supervision.
references: R22 POH Sec 10: PILOT KNOWLEDGE AND PROFICIENCY (p.10-5)
